cards.card_text: Instead, he takes it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
cards.verse_text: So he was unwilling to move the ark of the LORD to the City of David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.
cards.snippet: …David; instead, he took it aside to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite.

cards.card_text: The king stops at the last house while all his servants march past him: the Cherethites and Pelethites, men under David's command, plus six hundred Gittites who followed him from Gath.
cards.verse_text: He stopped at the last house, and all his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.
cards.snippet: …his servants marched past him—all the Cherethites and Pelethites, and six hundred Gittites who had followed him from Gath.

cards.card_text: Then David tells Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner and an exile who arrived only yesterday, to go back and stay with the new king.
cards.verse_text: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us?
cards.snippet: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why should you also go with us?

cards.card_text: He splits the army in three: one third under Joab, one under Joab's brother Abishai, and one under Ittai the Gittite, a foreigner loyal to David (2 Samuel 15:19-21).
cards.verse_text: He sent out the troops, a third under Joab, a third under Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite.
cards.snippet: …Joab’s brother Abishai son of Zeruiah, and a third under Ittai the Gittite.

cards.verse_text: Once again there was a battle with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam.

cards.card_text: That's "…the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the shaft of whose spear was like a weaver's beam." Next comes a battle at Gath, with a man of great stature, and something unusual is going on with his hands and feet.
